A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Basque LLM adaptation study. All 25 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark results, safety/bias evaluations and an arena study collecting 12,890 preferences from 1,680 participants.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main experimental findings and detailed benchmark and human-evaluation results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The Llama 3.1 backbones, synthetic-instruction generation and translation procedures, and corpus/instruction training combinations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora and instructions, 27 benchmark evaluations across Basque, English and Spanish, human arena scenarios, and safety/bias datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including the backbone-derived variants, Llama 3.1 Instruct, GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Llama-eus remains explicitly excluded.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training budgets, hyperparameters, benchmark procedures, arena sampling settings and safety/bias protocols are identical. The revised computing acknowledgement does not establish any experimental-setting change.

E4.justification: The component comparisons, benchmark–arena correlations, cross-language trade-offs, safety/bias analyses, manual instruction assessment and Appendix B instruction-count/epoch study are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 90% confidence intervals for Bradley–Terry scores and the same safety-annotation agreement statistics. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout, including Tables 1–2 and 6–9 and Figures 3–5 and 12. No result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The configuration-space formalization in Section 4 and Bradley–Terry definitions and scoring equations in Appendix C.2 are identical. No theoretical additions or revisions appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about target-language corpora, synthetic instructions, instruction-tuned backbones and competitive Basque models, together with the same released-resource contributions.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged, including cross-language trade-offs, alignment retention and limitations concerning language/model scope, preference alignment and contamination analysis.

D1.justification: The acknowledgements add EuroHPC allocation EHPC-AI-2024A04-074 for BSC MareNostrum 5, refining computing-access provenance. Appendix B already documents both MareNostrum 5 and CINECA Leonardo and their training roles; hardware specifications, training details and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography content and research positioning are identical. References that cross different page boundaries in v3 have only reflowed.

P1.justification: The computing acknowledgement is locally rewritten, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Scientific prose, terminology and section ordering are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgement moves the References heading from the bottom-left to the top-right column on page 10 and slightly reflows the bibliography through page 13. All figures and tables remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 refines computing credit and slightly reflows the bibliography. Appendix B already supplied the hardware information, while methods, experimental evidence, claims, limitations and reproducibility settings remain unchanged. The limited attribution update does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
